questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The dimensional formula of the coefficient of viscosity is:
questions.explanation: From F = ηA(dv/dx), η = F dx/(A dv) = [MLT⁻²][L]/([L²][LT⁻¹]) = [ML⁻¹T⁻¹]. Its SI unit is the poiseuille or pascal second.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 1: Units and Measurements

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The quantisation of electric charge means that the charge on any body:
options: Is always an integral multiple of the elementary charge e
questions.explanation: q = ne, where e is 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. Because e is so small, charge appears continuous at the everyday scale, just as matter appears continuous despite being made of atoms.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 12, Chapter 1: Electric Charges and Fields

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The energy equivalent of one atomic mass unit is approximately:
questions.explanation: Putting 1 u = 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ kg into E = mc² gives about 931 MeV, which is why mass defects of a fraction of a u release millions of electron volts.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Ostwald's dilution law applies to the dissociation of:
options: Weak electrolytes, relating the degree of dissociation to the dissociation constant and concentration
questions.explanation: For a weak electrolyte Ka = cα²/(1 - α), and when α is small this simplifies to α = √(Ka/c), so dilution raises the degree of dissociation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Interstitial compounds formed by transition metals with small atoms such as hydrogen, carbon and nitrogen are characteristically:
options: Hard, with high melting points and chemically rather inert
questions.explanation: The small atoms slip into the holes of the metal lattice and lock it, so steel, which is an interstitial compound of iron and carbon, is much harder than pure iron.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 12, Chapter 4: The d- and f-Block Elements

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is a correct difference between DNA and RNA?
options: DNA has ribose and uracil, RNA has deoxyribose and thymine
DNA has deoxyribose and thymine, RNA has ribose and uracil
questions.explanation: The missing 2' hydroxyl group makes DNA chemically more stable, which is why it is the better store of genetic information while RNA acts as the working copy.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: A sieve tube element of the phloem is always accompanied by a companion cell because the sieve tube:
options: Loses its nucleus at maturity and depends on the companion cell to control its activity
questions.explanation: The two are linked by many plasmodesmata, and the companion cell also helps load sugars into the sieve tube for long distance transport.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 6: Anatomy of Flowering Plants

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Agrobacterium tumefaciens is widely used in plant genetic engineering because it:
options: Naturally transfers a part of its Ti plasmid into the plant genome, and so can act as a vector
questions.explanation: The tumour causing genes are removed and the genes of interest put in their place, so the disarmed plasmid delivers the desired gene instead of causing crown gall disease.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 9: Biotechnology: Principles and Processes

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The two cerebral hemispheres of the human brain are connected by a thick band of nerve fibres called the:
questions.explanation: The corpus callosum lets the two halves share information. The cerebral cortex above it holds the motor, sensory and association areas.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 18: Neural Control and Coordination

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Cannabinoids, obtained from the inflorescences of Cannabis sativa, act mainly on which organ system when abused?
options: The cardiovascular system, along with their effects on the brain
questions.explanation: They bind receptors mainly in the brain, and abuse is known to affect the heart and blood vessels. Marijuana, hashish, charas and ganja all come from this plant.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 7: Human Health and Disease
